explanation: Scurvy comes from a lack of vitamin C. Dogs and cats make their own, but humans, apes, monkeys and guinea pigs must get it from food.

claims.text: Eating citrus fruit prevents scurvy, which is caused by a lack of vitamin C.
Rickets, beriberi and pellagra are caused by a lack of vitamin D, thiamine and niacin respectively, not vitamin C.
Dogs and cats can make their own vitamin C, while humans, other apes, monkeys and guinea pigs cannot and must get it from their diet.

evidence.restatement: Scurvy is caused by lack of vitamin C, which citrus fruit supplies.
Rickets comes from lack of vitamin D, beriberi from lack of thiamine and pellagra from lack of niacin.
Dogs and cats make their own vitamin C; humans, other apes, monkeys and guinea pigs lack the enzyme and need it in food.
Scurvy is caused by a lack of vitamin C, and citrus fruit prevents it.

claimResults.note: The other three are also vitamin deficiencies, which makes them fair distractors; only scurvy is a vitamin C disease.

evidence.restatement: Rickets comes from a lack of vitamin D (and calcium), beriberi from thiamine and pellagra from niacin.
